title: The Impact of Single-Task E-Paper Displays on Emotion, Cognition, and Performance in Knowledge Workers
content: This study investigates the cognitive and affective differences between using an E-paper tablet (reMarkable) and a traditional computer for knowledge work-related tasks. Sixty participants were pseudo-randomly assigned to either an E-paper tablet group or a computer group, and performed tasks involving reading, learning, creativity, multitasking, and memory recall. Electroencephalography (EEG) brain monitoring and Heart-Rate Variability (HRV) measurements were used to evaluate cognitive load, stress, vigilance, and focus. Behavioral measures of creativity and learning were assessed. The results suggest that the use of an E-paper tablet can dramatically enhance focus, reduce stress, and improve creativity compared to traditional computers. This study provides evidence that using E-paper technology for knowledge work may lead to improved cognitive outcomes and user satisfaction.
